most_serious.finding: "With no overdraw given" is true of the start only. The rise that ends the line is itself a premise, and with the cap on the level it gives the ending in two lines. No new statement concludes an overdraw; the conclusion is the ending. Telling it as "the lock brings an overdraw about" would say more than the Lean.
most_serious.evidence: l.655 `(rises : ∀ j, use (Law.orbit alone w j) < use (Law.orbit alone w (j + 1)))`: a premise on the course of the way as it was, at every step, blind to the level, without bound. With l.653 `(keeps : RegimeMargin.Keeps giving 0 hi)` and l.654 `(high : x ≤ hi)` the level never passes hi while the use at step j is at least j (private `rises_from`, l.614); so at step hi the use takes the whole level and by `nothing` the next level is nothing. On the lock the rise is given state-wise, l.1390-1391 `(more : ∀ v : A × R × Nat, P.le w.1 v.1 → M.le w.2.1 v.2.1 → use v < use (windowAlone fA hA reads v))`; the lock premises only turn `more` into `rises` (l.1396-1398, through `locked_alone_not_below`). `count_rises` derives `more` from two further givens, l.1416 `(rise : ∀ a g, favours g → a < fA a g)` and l.1417 `(count : ∀ v, use v = v.1 * u)`; in Three both hold by the definitions of riseShare and drawerUse (l.2878 `Nat.lt_succ_self a`, l.2879 `Nat.mul_one v.1`). Header l.288-290: "the sentence above that nothing here derives an overdraw from a lock holds of `locked_ends_with_net_regime` and `locked_ends_on_window`, not of `locked_ends_rising`, where the rise of the use is given as `more`". What the lock derives there is that the course stays where `more` is asked. The two docstrings do name `rises` and `more` as given (l.648-649, l.1377).

most_serious.finding: `more` does not ask that the use read the share or the rule. A use that reads only the step count meets it on any lock, with the share never moving. "The rise of the use with the share" is the count case's reading, not the law.
